difficulty.from: question type (application); the RC bank has no difficulty field

answer.text: A search team finds a wreck where a careful sonar survey and a historian's bold guess overlap
answer.line: Paragraph 12: the double helix came where patient measurement met bold guessing, and neither would have finished alone. The wreck has both.

steps: Name the principle before reading the choices. Paragraph 12, sentence 4: two methods, patient measurement and bold guessing, neither enough alone.
Look for the case that needs both at once. A careful survey and a bold guess meeting is that case.
Cross off the halves. Measurement alone and guessing alone each leave the job unfinished.

choices.text: A detective solves a case from a single photograph that happens to show the culprit's face clearly
choices.note: Paragraph 12 opens on how little a single image could settle. This case runs the principle backward.

choices.text: Two rival laboratories race toward the same result, and only the faster one is remembered
choices.note: A race for credit echoes the debate in paragraphs 10 and 11, not the two methods meeting in paragraph 12.

choices.text: A surveyor refuses to publish a map until every hill has been measured twice
choices.note: Measurement alone is only half the principle. Paragraph 12 says patient measurement would not have finished the job alone.

choices.text: A search team finds a wreck where a careful sonar survey and a historian's bold guess overlap
choices.note: Careful survey plus bold guess, and the find comes where they meet.

choices.text: A theorist's guess about a planet's orbit is accepted without any measurement
choices.note: Guessing with no measurement is only the other half. The passage says bold guessing alone would not finish the job either.
